where: Section 2 table and worked example step 6, exam traps
problem: Exponents and subscripts are typed as plain characters, so the quadratic factor reads (jω/ωn)2 and the phase reads −tan−1(ω), which a student can misread as multiplication or as 'tan minus one'. The same applies to log10.
fix: Use the inline tags: (jω/ωn)<sup>2</sup>, −tan<sup>−1</sup>(ω), log<sub>10</sub>, so the phone rendering is unambiguous.

problem: The answer gives the form K(1+s/20)/(s(1+s/2)) but never says how K is fixed, so a student may think the slope pattern alone determines the transfer function.
fix: Add one line: K is fixed by the low-frequency line, which must pass through −20 dB/decade at the measured gain at some reference ω; slopes give only the pole-zero pattern, not K.
